verdict.rationale: Weave's docs state that you can evaluate application responses using LLM judges and custom scorers. Scorers take outputs and return metric dictionaries, can be written as function- or class-based custom scorers, and an agent-evaluation guide is scored with an LLM judge. missing for 10: explicit documentation of how the LLM-judge model, prompt and rubric are configured, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can score outputs with configurable LLM-as-a-judge evaluators

citations.quote: Evaluate your agent’s or application’s responses using LLM judges and custom scorers
Evaluate single-turn and multi-turn AI agents in Weave using the agents workflow and EvaluationLogger, scored with an LLM judge.
In Weave, Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics. They take the AI’s output, analyze it, and return a dictionary of results.
Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.
Custom Scorers let you encode evaluation criteria that are specific to your use case, beyond what the built-in Scorers cover.
